stories.title: Create /privacy-policy page with PDPA Section 7 compliant content
stories.description: Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (PDPA) Section 7 requires a privacy notice disclosing what personal data is collected, the purpose of collection, and user rights to access/correct data. The site currently collects guest emails via the newsletter form and processes analytics via GA4, but has no privacy policy page. This is a legal compliance requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: A /privacy-policy route exists and returns a 200 with full page content

Page discloses: data categories collected (name, email, IP, cookies), processing purposes (booking, analytics, marketing), third-party processors (GA4, Sentry), data retention periods, and user rights (access, correction, withdrawal)
Footer contains a visible 'Privacy Policy' link pointing to /privacy-policy
CookieConsent banner links to /privacy-policy
Page includes Data Controller contact details and registration note per PDPA
generateMetadata sets canonical, noindex:false, and descriptive title/description
technicalNotes: Create site/src/app/privacy-policy/page.tsx
PDPA 2010 Section 7 — notice and choice principle: https://www.pdp.gov.my/
Reference GDPR Article 13/14 equivalents for EU visitors already covered by cookie consent
Add link in site/src/components/Footer.tsx and site/src/components/CookieConsent.tsx

stories.title: Implement prefers-reduced-motion across all CSS and JS animations
stories.description: Users with vestibular disorders, epilepsy, or motion sensitivity rely on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` to suppress animations. WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) and WCAG 2.2.2 (AA) both have related requirements, and Google's Lighthouse audits flag missing reduced-motion support. The site uses Tailwind transitions and scroll-triggered effects that need to respect this OS-level preference.
acceptanceCriteria: All CSS transition and animation classes are wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` or overridden inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`
In globals.css, a root-level block sets animation-duration, animation-iteration-count, transition-duration to near-zero and scroll-behavior to auto for reduced motion users
Any JS-driven scroll animation (intersection observers for fade-in) checks `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` and skips animations if true
Lighthouse accessibility audit passes with no motion-related flags
Visual appearance on hover/focus states is preserved — only motion is removed, not styling
technicalNotes: Add to site/src/app/globals.css: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; } }
WCAG Technique C39: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C39
Check Hero.tsx, Gallery.tsx, Destinations.tsx for any JS animation or intersection observer fade-in classes

stories.title: Audit and fix WCAG 1.4.3 color contrast failures across all components
stories.description: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (Level AA) requires a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Common failure points include amber/orange CTAs on white, grey placeholder text, badge text on coloured backgrounds, and footer links. A systematic audit using automated tooling followed by targeted fixes ensures the site meets AA compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: All normal text (under 18pt / 14pt bold) achieves at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background
All large text and UI component boundaries achieve at least 3:1 contrast
Zero contrast errors reported by axe-core or Lighthouse accessibility audit
Amber/orange button text is darkened or the button background adjusted to meet 4.5:1 — amber-500 (#f59e0b on white = 2.26:1) fails and must be replaced
Grey placeholder text in forms meets 4.5:1 (typically requires #767676 or darker on white)
technicalNotes: Run Lighthouse Accessibility audit or axe DevTools to enumerate all failures first
Use WebAIM Contrast Checker: https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/
Tailwind amber-700 (#b45309) on white = 5.01:1 passes; amber-500 (#f59e0b) on white = 2.26:1 fails
Fix badge foreground/background pairs in BlogCard.tsx, BlogFilter.tsx, and category pages
WCAG 1.4.3: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html

stories.title: Add GeoCoordinates to LodgingBusiness schema for Google Maps local pack
stories.description: The existing LodgingBusiness JSON-LD in StructuredData.tsx is missing a `geo` property with precise latitude and longitude. Google uses GeoCoordinates for local pack positioning, Maps integration, and Knowledge Panel accuracy. Hostelworld and Booking.com listings already have coordinates, so the website's structured data should match to improve local SEO.
acceptanceCriteria: LodgingBusiness JSON-LD in StructuredData.tsx includes a `geo` property of type `GeoCoordinates`
GeoCoordinates contains `latitude` and `longitude` with at least 5 decimal places matching the physical address
The `address` PostalAddress object includes `addressCountry: 'MY'`, `postalCode`, `addressLocality: 'Johor Bahru'`, and `addressRegion: 'Johor'`
Google Rich Results Test validates the updated schema without errors
The coordinates match the pin location on Google Maps for the hostel
technicalNotes: Edit site/src/components/StructuredData.tsx — add geo: { '@type': 'GeoCoordinates', latitude: X.XXXXX, longitude: Y.YYYYY }
Schema.org GeoCoordinates: https://schema.org/GeoCoordinates
Google LocalBusiness structured data docs: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/local-business
Verify coordinates match Google Business Profile pin to avoid NAP inconsistency

stories.title: Apply rate limiting middleware to /api/public and /api/chat proxy routes
stories.description: The Next.js site proxies booking API calls (/api/public/*) and Rainbow AI chat (/api/chat/*) to the admin server. These endpoints have no rate limiting, making them vulnerable to DoS attacks, credential stuffing, and API abuse. OWASP API Security Top 10 item API4:2023 (Unrestricted Resource Consumption) specifically covers this risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Requests to /api/public/* are limited to 30 requests per minute per IP; excess requests receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header
Requests to /api/chat/* are limited to 20 requests per minute per IP; excess requests receive HTTP 429
Rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) are present on API responses
Legitimate users completing a normal booking flow are not rate-limited
Rate limiting is implemented at the Edge in site/src/middleware.ts before the proxy rewrite executes
technicalNotes: Implement in site/src/middleware.ts using @upstash/ratelimit with Upstash Redis free tier, or use a simple in-memory sliding window with next-rate-limit for zero-infrastructure option
OWASP API4:2023: https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa4-unrestricted-resource-consumption/
Next.js Middleware docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/middleware
Upstash ratelimit: https://github.com/upstash/ratelimit-js

stories.title: Add static OG images for /rooms, /amenities, and /guide pages
stories.description: Blog posts already have dynamic OG images via next/og ImageResponse, but the key conversion pages (/rooms, /amenities, /guide) fall back to the generic site-wide OG image. Unique per-page OG images increase click-through rates by 2-3x on social shares and appear correctly in WhatsApp link previews. WhatsApp requires images under 200 KB for reliable CDN delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: /rooms page has a unique OG image showing capsule pod photography with 'Capsule Rooms from RM35/night' text overlay
/amenities page has a unique OG image with relevant facilities photography
/guide page has a unique OG image with JB skyline/landmark and 'Johor Bahru Backpacker Guide' text
Each page's generateMetadata exports openGraph.images with width: 1200, height: 630, and alt text
All three OG images are under 200 KB
og:image:alt is populated with descriptive text on all three pages
technicalNotes: Option A: Create static PNG/JPEG files at site/public/images/og-rooms.jpg, og-amenities.jpg, og-guide.jpg
Option B: Use next/og opengraph-image.tsx convention per route (matches pattern used by blog)
Update generateMetadata in site/src/app/rooms/page.tsx, amenities/page.tsx, guide/page.tsx
Test with: https://opengraphdebug.com/ and share on WhatsApp to verify thumbnail
Next.js opengraph-image file convention: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/opengraph-image

stories.title: Add TouristAttraction schema markup to /guide page for JB attractions
stories.description: The /guide page lists major Johor Bahru attractions and activities for backpackers but has no structured data. Adding TouristAttraction (or Place) schema with name, description, and geo coordinates for each listed attraction enables rich snippets in search and helps Google understand the page as a destination guide, boosting its local SEO value and authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Each major attraction section on /guide has a corresponding TouristAttraction JSON-LD block with @type, name, description, and geo (GeoCoordinates)
Minimum 5 attractions are marked up with TouristAttraction schema
A BreadcrumbList schema is present on the /guide page (Home > Guide)
Google Rich Results Test shows no errors for the /guide page markup
Structured data is injected via <script type='application/ld+json'> scoped to the page component, not globally in layout
technicalNotes: Create a GuideStructuredData component or inline JSON-LD in site/src/app/guide/page.tsx
Schema.org TouristAttraction: https://schema.org/TouristAttraction
Attractions to include: Johor Bahru City Square, Danga Bay, KSL City Mall, Arulmigu Raja Mariamman Temple, Johor Bahru Old Chinese Temple
Can use @type: ['TouristAttraction', 'Place'] for broader matching

stories.title: Add Event schema to CommunityEvents component for Google event rich results
stories.description: The CommunityEvents component displays hostel and local JB events on the homepage but has no Event structured data. Adding Event JSON-LD enables Google to display event rich results (date, location, ticket link) in the SERP event carousel, increasing click-through for event-related queries such as 'things to do in JB this weekend'.
acceptanceCriteria: Each event rendered by CommunityEvents has a corresponding Event JSON-LD with: @type: 'Event', name, startDate (ISO 8601), endDate, location (Place with address), description, and organizer
Events use eventAttendanceMode: 'https://schema.org/OfflineEventAttendanceMode' for in-person events
Events use eventStatus: 'https://schema.org/EventScheduled'
Google Rich Results Test validates Event markup with no critical errors
Past events (startDate < today) are excluded from the JSON-LD output to avoid stale data warnings
technicalNotes: Edit site/src/components/CommunityEvents.tsx to inject per-event <script type='application/ld+json'>
Schema.org Event: https://schema.org/Event
Google Event rich results docs: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event
Filter events array before building JSON-LD: events.filter(e => new Date(e.startDate) >= new Date())

stories.title: Set up Lighthouse CI in GitHub Actions for automated performance budgets
stories.description: Without automated Lighthouse checks, performance regressions (bundle bloat, new render-blocking resources, CLS shifts) go undetected until after deployment. Lighthouse CI on GitHub Actions runs audits on every PR and fails the check if scores drop below defined thresholds, creating a continuous performance safety net for the website.
acceptanceCriteria: A .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml workflow file exists and triggers on pull_request to master/main
Workflow builds the Next.js app, starts it on a local port, and runs lhci autorun against the homepage, /rooms, and /blog URLs
Lighthouse CI fails the build if: Performance < 80, Accessibility < 90, Best Practices < 90, SEO < 90
A lighthouserc.json config file exists at the repo root with the above assertions and numberOfRuns: 3
Workflow results appear as a named GitHub status check on each PR
technicalNotes: Install: npm install --save-dev @lhci/cli
@lhci/cli package and docs: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse-ci
Use treoshark/lighthouse-ci-action from GitHub Marketplace for simplified setup
web.dev Lighthouse CI guide: https://web.dev/articles/lighthouse-ci
numberOfRuns: 3 reduces variance from system load fluctuations

stories.title: Upgrade web-vitals to v4 and report INP attribution breakdown to GA4
stories.description: The current GA4 integration via @next/third-parties captures page views but not Core Web Vitals breakdown data. Web Vitals v4's attribution build provides INP sub-component data (inputDelay, processingTime, presentationDelay) and LoAF (Long Animation Frames) that pinpoint which interactions are slow. Sending this to GA4 as custom events enables data-driven INP optimization.
acceptanceCriteria: The web-vitals package is version 4.x in package.json
A 'use client' component imports from web-vitals/attribution and registers onINP, onLCP, onCLS handlers
Each metric fires a GA4 custom event via gtag with: metric_name, metric_value, metric_id, and for INP: input_delay, processing_time, presentation_delay, interaction_target
Events appear in GA4 DebugView as web_vitals events with correct parameters
The reporter component is loaded with next/dynamic (ssr: false) to avoid SSR issues
technicalNotes: npm install web-vitals@^4
web-vitals v4 CHANGELOG: https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
Attribution import: import { onINP } from 'web-vitals/attribution'
Create site/src/components/WebVitalsReporter.tsx as a 'use client' component loaded in layout.tsx
Use navigator.sendBeacon for reliable metric delivery on page unload

stories.title: Add @next/bundle-analyzer and enforce 250 KB initial JS budget per route
stories.description: As the site grows, JavaScript bundles can silently balloon with new dependencies. Without a bundle analyzer, there is no visibility into what contributes to load time. Setting a 250 KB initial JS budget for the homepage (Google's recommended threshold) and running analysis in CI prevents future regressions caused by unnoticed large imports.
acceptanceCriteria: @next/bundle-analyzer is installed as a dev dependency and wired into next.config.ts
Running ANALYZE=true npm run build opens a bundle treemap in the browser
A size-limit config in package.json defines a 250 KB budget for the main JS chunk and CI fails on breach
The three largest current bundle contributors are documented in a comment in next.config.ts
Sentry SDK tree-shaking is verified to be working (no unused Sentry modules in bundle)
technicalNotes: npm install --save-dev @next/bundle-analyzer
@next/bundle-analyzer docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/optimizing/bundle-analyzer
Wrap in next.config.ts: withBundleAnalyzer({ enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true' })(nextConfig)
size-limit for CI enforcement: https://github.com/ai/size-limit
Sentry tree-shaking guide: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/configuration/tree-shaking/

stories.title: Add honeypot field to contact form to block spam bot submissions
stories.description: The contact form at /contact has no bot protection. Spam bots that auto-fill all form fields will submit noise or malicious payloads. A CSS-hidden honeypot field (visible to bots that ignore CSS, invisible to real users) is a zero-friction, privacy-respecting alternative to reCAPTCHA that adds no third-party script, no cookie consent requirement, and no user friction.
acceptanceCriteria: The contact form includes a hidden input field (e.g., name='website') styled with position: absolute; left: -9999px; opacity: 0 so real users cannot see or interact with it
The field has aria-hidden='true' and tabIndex={-1} to exclude it from keyboard navigation and screen readers
Server-side handling rejects (returns 400 or silently drops) any submission where the honeypot field is non-empty
Legitimate form submissions from real users are unaffected
No third-party scripts (reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha) are added to the page
technicalNotes: Edit site/src/app/contact/page.tsx or the form component it uses
Honeypot pattern reference: https://css-tricks.com/fighting-spam-with-honeypots/
Add a <label> pointing to the honeypot field with visually-hidden text to confuse advanced bots that look for unlabelled fields
Combine with rate limiting (separate story) for layered bot protection

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7: Audit and comply with Redundant Entry requirement
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (Level A, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that information previously entered by the user in the same process is auto-populated or available for selection, avoiding cognitive burden of re-entering data. Any multi-step booking or enquiry flow on the site must comply with this new baseline Level A requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: All forms on the site are audited for fields requesting the same data type more than once (e.g., email + confirm email) — duplicate-entry fields are either removed or auto-populated
If a confirm email field exists in the contact form, it uses browser autocomplete='email' pairing and is justified in a code comment
If the booking flow (proxied admin SPA) has multi-step data re-entry, it is documented as out-of-scope with a ticket raised to the admin team
A WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 compliance note is added to the accessibility section of project documentation
Manual audit checklist passes with no violations in the site's own forms
technicalNotes: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Understanding: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html
Check site/src/app/contact/page.tsx for all form fields
Correct autocomplete attribute values per spec: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill
The /book route is a proxy — SC 3.3.7 compliance there is the admin SPA's responsibility

stories.title: Enable Turbopack in next dev script for faster local development startup
stories.description: Next.js 15 ships Turbopack stable for development. It delivers up to 76.7% faster local server startup and 96.3% faster Fast Refresh compared to Webpack. Enabling it via the `--turbo` flag on the dev script is a zero-risk, zero-config developer experience improvement with no production impact.
acceptanceCriteria: The dev script in site/package.json is updated to include the --turbo flag: 'next dev --turbo'
Running npm run dev starts the server using Turbopack (confirmed by terminal output showing 'Turbopack')
No TypeScript errors or missing module errors appear that were not present before enabling Turbopack
All existing pages load correctly in development mode with Turbopack
A comment in package.json or CLAUDE.md notes that Turbopack is dev-only; production builds still use Webpack
technicalNotes: Edit site/package.json scripts.dev from 'next dev' to 'next dev --turbo'
Next.js 15 Turbopack stable blog: https://nextjs.org/blog/turbopack-for-development-stable
Turbopack docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/architecture/turbopack
Production build (next build) still uses Webpack — Turbopack production support is a future release

stories.title: Add CSP violation reporting via report-uri directive to Sentry
stories.description: The Content Security Policy is already implemented in enforce mode, but without a `report-uri` directive, CSP violations are silent — they block threats but provide no forensic data. Sentry (already installed) provides a dedicated CSP report endpoint. Adding the report-uri directive routes all violation reports into the existing Sentry project, enabling monitoring of injection attempts and misconfigured third-party scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: The CSP header in next.config.ts includes a report-uri directive pointing to the Sentry security endpoint
The Sentry CSP report URI is stored in an environment variable NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_CSP_REPORT_URI or SENTRY_CSP_REPORT_URI rather than hard-coded
Deliberately triggering a CSP violation in a development/staging environment produces a report in Sentry under Security Issues
Existing CSP enforcement (blocking behaviour) is unaffected — only reporting is added
Environment variable is documented in .env.example or project README
technicalNotes: Sentry CSP reporting docs: https://docs.sentry.io/product/security-policy-reporting/
Sentry security endpoint format: https://o<org-id>.ingest.sentry.io/api/<project-id>/security/?sentry_key=<public-key>
Add report-uri directive to cspHeader array in site/next.config.ts
Can also use report-to + Report-To header for newer Reporting API (browsers are migrating from report-uri to report-to)
